description: The writer, the valley and the walks.

settings.heading: A valley, two buses, one café
settings.standfirst: Nell Harker walks slowly and writes about towns, weather and the paths between them.

settings.heading: A valley with one café and two buses a day
settings.body:
I write about towns, weather and the paths between them, mostly on foot and mostly slowly.

The journal started as notes for myself. It became letters when people started asking where the closed path went.

settings.heading: Why the walks are slow
settings.body:
I started walking the valley paths the year the bus timetable halved. There was no plan in it, only a need to get to the shop and back, and the shop was four miles away by the road and three by the fields.

The fields are slower, and that is the point. A road tells you where to look; a field path lets you choose, and most days I choose the hedge, the sky over the ridge and whoever is coming the other way.

What to bring

  • Boots that have been rained on before
  • A map, even though it leaves things out
  • Something to eat at the stile, out of the wind

Letters are welcome, and I answer every one. The address is on the contact page, along with the hours I keep.

settings.quote: Nobody has taken it down because nobody is quite sure whose job that is.
settings.attribution: Nell Harker, The path above the town

settings.heading: A letter when there is something to say
settings.text: Usually once a month. Never more than twice.
settings.note: One click to leave. Your address goes nowhere else.
